The technique was proposed in a 2012 Stack Overflow answer by Mikael Emtinger for rendering animated voxel scenes in WebGL using Three.js or GLOW [S1, unofficial].

The evidence (Source [S1]) is a Stack Overflow answer posted by Mikael Emtinger on August 23, 2012. The answer explicitly discusses rendering a 128x128x128 voxel grid using WebGL. It details the technique of packing voxel data into 4 separate 128x128 RGBA images (where each pixel represents 32 voxels along the Z-axis). It mentions using vertex texture fetch in the vertex shader to determine voxel presence. It also compares Three.js and GLOW, suggesting GLOW as a cleaner alternative for this specific approach involving drawArrays. All specific facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

Extract the bit corresponding to the vertex's local Z-index (0–31) from the sampled pixel using floating-point manipulation [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that bit operations (shift, and, or) are not available in WebGL and that integers are not supported on some Mac drivers. Consequently, it advises to 'Avoid using ints; use floating-point sampling and manipulation instead.' This directly supports the claim that one should use floating-point manipulation to extract the bit.

*   **Input:** A vertex buffer containing vertex attributes [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the technical details provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly mentions: 1) The grid resolution is 128x128x128 (approx 2 million points). 2) The data storage method involves 4 PNG images (128x128 pixels, RGBA, 32 bits per pixel, 1 bit per voxel). 3) Vertex attributes include vertex/normal attributes and a parallel attribute for UVs and bit information (3D UV-coordinate). 4) An alternative method uses a 3D UV-coordinate and vertex index in the .w component. 5) The vertex shader uses vertex texture fetch to sample bits and cull invisible vertices. 6) WebGL lacks native bit operations and integer support on some drivers, requiring floating-point manipulation. 7) Vertex texture fetch is required but not universally supported. 8) GLOW is suggested as a cleaner alternative to Three.js for this specific approach.
